card.title: PlayStation 4 Controller Sync, Safe Mode & WiFi/Bluetooth Issues

claims.statement: If wireless controllers do not sync in the dashboard but connect when plugged in via USB in Safe Mode, the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth IC or its firmware/NOR integration is faulty.
claims.evidence: Safe mode bypasses wireless modules and relies entirely on USB data for controller communication.
claims.quote: If the controllers do not sync in safe mode, then the NOR flash IC could be faulty. Connect controller with USB cable and see if the controllers are syncing in Safe mode. if its get’s connected then you know there could

claims.statement: Error SU-41283-8 indicates a problem with the Wi-Fi IC.
claims.evidence: Error code correlation to wireless subsystem failures.
claims.quote: Error SU-41283-8 Problem with the Wifi ic.

claims.statement: Error CE-35888-2 typically indicates a Renesas or MediaTek disc drive IC problem that is unrepairable if it persists after update and mechanical inspection.
claims.evidence: Chipset limitation within the Blu-ray subsystem causing update/hardware mismatch errors.
claims.quote: Error CE-35888-2 While the disc drive itself may be functioning, encountering this error typically indicates a Renesas IC problem, which is not repairable.

procedure: Connect controller with a USB cable and test syncing in Safe Mode.
Update the system firmware to attempt repair of corrupted NOR software linked to wireless modules.
Inspect Blu-ray drive mechanics and replace drive if error CE-35888-2 persists after update.
card.caveats: Safe mode connection uses USB protocol, whereas dashboard connection uses wireless modules.
